source.title: A priori generalization error for two-layer ReLU neural network through minimum norm solution
source.authors: Zhi-Qin John Xu; Jiwei Zhang; Yaoyu Zhang; Cheng-Chao Zhao

record.tranche_reason: The paper derives a priori generalization error bounds for minimum-norm two-layer ReLU networks, but does not test any listed version's empirical claims about memorization, width sweeps, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness, or removing examples.
record.gate_note: The theorems are analytical bounds, not results from applying or measuring the interventions named in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper derives expected squared-risk bounds for minimum-norm and gradient-trained two-layer ReLU networks. It does not establish any listed version's behavioral comparison. In particular, a bound with a decreasing width-dependent term does not establish that actual test error keeps decreasing beyond interpolation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate, but combines distinct results. The authors first bound expected risk for finite-width minimum-norm solutions, then connect these to NTK solutions and sufficiently wide gradient-trained networks using cited approximation results. They conclude that small bounds need no added loss regularization or exponentially many neurons, under their stated assumptions; the gradient-training result additionally requires inputs on the unit sphere.
record.recipe_differences: The paper derives theoretical bounds for minimum-norm solutions and connects them to gradient training; it does not run the empirical recipes described in the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 5.2 bounds expected squared risk for minimum-distance-to-initialization solutions under bounded, finite-spectral-norm targets. Theorems 5.3 and 5.6 extend the analysis to width-dependent bounds and sufficiently wide gradient-trained networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated target, initialization, and width assumptions, two-layer ReLU networks admit a priori expected-risk bounds with width-dependent terms that vanish as width increases.

record.problems: The evidence is theoretical and depends on stated assumptions, including a bounded target function with finite spectral norm; it does not empirically measure a training–test gap.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization in the same training recipe, including chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Actual test-error changes when widening networks beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance under different tuning and training recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Theorems 5.3 and 5.6 are additional theoretical results outside the listed versions, so their omission does not require a missing entry. Citations to original generalization studies supply motivation rather than new tests.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance.
A width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Comparisons of convolutional and fully connected networks.
Large-batch and small-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Sharpness measurements and their relation to generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized training examples and its effect on test accuracy.
